title: How to find your thing
summary: Shaan Puri and Sam Parr argue that 'follow your passion' is bad advice and offer a replacement framework: follow your bliss/blisters (enduring enthusiasm plus willingness to suffer for it), pick a sales motion or 'loop' you love rather than an industry, and use the top regrets of the dying as a sanity check. They unpack the etymology of 'passion' (from suffering), Joseph Campbell's bliss/blisters reframe, Paul Graham's 'enthusiasm as motor and rudder,' and Cal Newport's 'passion as a byproduct of mastery.' Shaan shares his personal loop (curiosity → research → share top 1% with like-minded people) and Sam pushes back that passion doesn't have to be your job — 'braces money' from a steady job can be the answer. The episode closes with practical heuristics: name the blisters upfront, learn the art of noticing your own disproportionate enthusiasm, and accept that holding onto grounded advice is what keeps you upright when the world whiplashes you.

title: The Real Reason SpaceX is Buying Cursor
summary: ByteMonk explains why SpaceX offered $60B for Cursor — and uses the deal as a frame to walk through how Cursor actually works under the hood. The strategic argument is that the 'interface layer' (Cursor) is becoming more defensible than the model layer, which gives xAI/SpaceX instant entry into agentic coding and a better story for its IPO. No code is written; this is a conceptual walkthrough.

title: TurboQuant: How KV Cache Compression Makes 16GB Machines Run Bigger LLMs
